**TLDR: roughly one H100-day (~$50–80 rented) for a full-context run over the whole dataset, or ~4 hours (~$10) if you cap context at 32k. A single 80 GB GPU is enough — Qwen3.5's hybrid attention makes "high context" much cheaper than it sounds. The pipeline now supports Qwen3.5-9B natively, smoke-tested end-to-end, with the vision tower provably untouched.**

First, what I verified before estimating (Qwen3.5 is past my cutoff): it's a March 2026 release, early-fusion multimodal, 262K native context, and — the key fact for your question — a hybrid architecture where only 8 of 32 text layers use full attention (GQA, 4 KV heads); the other 24 are Gated DeltaNet linear attention. So long-context cost scales near-linearly, KV cache is only ~32 KB/token, and there's no quadratic blowup even at 140k tokens.

**The actual workload, measured from your prepared data:** 1,234 per-turn examples; context length is median ~33k tokens, mean ~42k, p90 ~94k, max ~142k; ~53M context-tokens per epoch. Each example costs about 12·N·L FLOPs (rollout prefill+decode ≈ 2NL, teacher forward ≈ 2NL, student forward+backward+checkpoint-recompute ≈ 8NL), ≈ 4.7×10¹⁵ FLOPs at the mean length for N=9B. With 2–4 epochs being plenty for on-policy distillation:

| Run | Examples kept | Time per epoch (1× H100-80GB) | 3-epoch total | Rented cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Context capped at 16k | ~30% | ~30–45 min | ~2 h | ~$5 |
| Capped at 32k (config default) | ~50% | ~1–1.5 h | ~4 h | ~$10 |
| Full traces (up to 142k) | 100% | ~5–8 h | ~16–24 h | ~$50–80 |

Memory at the 142k worst case: ~18 GB weights + ~37 GB checkpointed activations + ~5 GB KV/logits ≈ 60 GB peak — fits one H100/A100-80GB. A 48 GB card (L40S/A6000 Ada) works capped around ~48k context; 24–32 GB consumer cards aren't realistic for a 9B at high context without QLoRA. Note the dominant cost isn't generation — it's re-prefilling those long contexts three times per example. The biggest speed lever is swapping HF `generate` for vLLM with prefix caching for rollouts (turns within a trace share huge prefixes), which cuts a few hours off the full run.

**What I changed and tested for Qwen3.5:**
- The trainer auto-detects `AutoModelForMultimodalLM` (with `AutoModelForCausalLM` fallback for plain Qwen3), and tool-call arguments are now passed as mappings, which Qwen3.5's stricter chat template requires (both smoke tests re-pass).
- New `configs/sdft-qwen3.5-9b.yaml` with 32k limits (raise `limits.max_prompt_tokens` toward 142k on an 80 GB card) and LoRA targeting the text trunk's linears including the DeltaNet projections (`in_proj_qkv`, `in_proj_z`, `out_proj`).
- **Multimodal retention is by construction**: vision modules live under `model.visual.*` with non-colliding names, so the adapter can't touch them — I ran the full loop on Qwen3.5-0.8B (same architecture) and confirmed the saved adapter has 300 tensors, all in `language_model`, zero in the vision tower. The reverse-KL-to-frozen-base objective further anchors text behavior. Still worth a before/after spot-check on a couple of image prompts after merging.
- Install `flash-linear-attention` and `causal-conv1d` before a real run, or the DeltaNet layers fall back to a slow torch path (you'll see the warning).

Sources: [Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B), [Qwen 3.5 deep dive (architecture/context)](https://trilogyai.substack.com/p/deep-dive-qwen-35-brings-native-multimodality), [llm-stats Qwen3.5-9B](https://llm-stats.com/models/qwen3.5-9b)
